title: Construction: four paid transfers for the signed connector (no new kappa)
body:
Charles Bethin's PR1637 signed 3×3 connector uses twelve child queries and six paid root transfers. This contribution supplies a **four-transfer word**, retaining all twelve queries, both arbitrary-dirty roots, source preservation and the complete output map. The two root-doubling passes disappear.

**Status: finite complex circuit construction and scoped minimum theorem; no new kappa.** At exactly twelve signed child queries, four transfers are minimal for arbitrary fixed **one-way** root shears over Q or C. A short-transfer height argument reduces the lower bound to Ross Richardson's PR944 one-root obstruction, freshly replayed over all 720 paths by two implementations. Opposite-direction shears, scaled queries, more child calls and selected-supplier admission remain outside the result.

Both fully expanded 2/3/4/5/6/7-factor fixtures use 300 factor calls and five borrowed dirty rows (two roots plus three child rows). Total instructions fall from 306 to 304. In the matched dense integer tape model, including changed port bindings, the saving is `24 L^3 + 4 L^2 + 20 L - 4` head moves for every integer `L>=1`, plus `2L` fewer source reads, target updates, additions, work clears, root doublings and root negations. These are exact model counts, not measured runtime. COST.md also gives port-specific tariffs and pays admission, preparation, control, full-row work and width.

Only `research/signed-connector-transfer-minimum/` is added. One offline command:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/signed-connector-transfer-minimum/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_SIGNED_CONNECTOR_FOUR_TRANSFERS queries=12 transfers=4 minimum_one_way=4 factor_calls=300 controls=44 no_new_kappa`.

Local verification passes:

- Registered Python 3.12 replay, ordinary and optimized runs, and a clean committed export.
- Free noncommutative short/expanded forward and inverse maps; all three symbolic short-transfer shapes and meaningful hypothesis controls.
- Separate integer matrix/tape implementation: 24 fixtures, 660 arbitrary-input basis columns per direction, six tape lengths, and factor-order/scratch-restoration mutations.
- 44 short-word semantic mutations, read-only relocation, and five actual on-disk corruption rejections.
- Original C++ discovery replay: 1,641,024 restored source traces completed through three transfers; stopped at the first four-transfer witness. No exhaustive length-four claim.
- `make selected-record-check`; selected record and `upstream/` unchanged. Full selected cold replay and hosted CI are separate, unclaimed gates.

Base: `858771bcca3b8dd5d4ef4aa682a13cc9b7e23920`. OS assignment seed **32**, complex-supplier track. PR1637 is pinned at `9bee6cc01f151b92ccfe147046855715843f066a`. The submission refresh fully paginated 593 open PRs and 291 Discussion records without warnings. Main's selected PR1094 record remained byte-identical at `1f7a934975e5eacaf83511c9ac870263bf095e05`.

Credit Charles Bethin / PR1637 for the two-root construction, twelve-query minimum, factor fixture and layout; Ross Richardson / PR944 for the target and one-root obstruction; martinxxx9 / PR1088 and Hanson Sun / PR1526 for the weighted/scaling predecessors. The proof extends woklerx's PR1438 source-port separation method from two XOR transfers to arbitrary characteristic-zero shears and the three-shear case. Gareth Davidson's PR1498 and Hanson Sun's PR1615 concern the different universal binary five-source target. Original notices and exact pins are retained.

Prepared for **Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance**. Separate implementations by the same AI agent; no independent human or proof-assistant review claimed. Apache-2.0. The README and TASK.json give explicit next questions and blockers.
